open_points.subject: M11 pending import confirmation disclosure class
open_points.text: The table classifies “the owner session, but for its uploaded import file” as `business_confidential`, while M11 stores pending-confirmation “inputs it is bound to” and A16 binds an import confirmation to “names, aliases and Customer values”; those inputs include fields the same table classifies as `personal_data`.
open_points.question: What class applies to personal-data values copied from the import file into the owner session’s pending confirmation?
options: Classify the pending confirmation by its highest bound input
Keep only a digest or opaque reference in the confirmation
Treat all pending-confirmation inputs as `business_confidential` despite their values
open_points.default_guess: Classify the pending confirmation as `personal_data` whenever any bound input is `personal_data`.

open_points.subject: M09 audit sequence after backup restore
open_points.text: M09 says sequence numbers are “never reused”, but A15 says that after restoring an older backup, numbers belonging to lost later entries “are issued again for new entries.”
open_points.question: Must audit sequence numbers remain unique across the real lifetime of the installation, including histories discarded by restore, or only within the restored store’s current history?
options: Never reuse a number even after restore
Reuse numbers lost by restoring an older history
Add a restored-history epoch so the complete identifier remains unique
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored store as a new history branch and reuse the lost numbers, while documenting that sequence numbers are unique only within a branch.

open_points.subject: M10 migration closure after restore
open_points.text: R0-79 says “after the first successful import the operation is closed and refused,” while M10 now says a restore from before the import yields a history in which the closure is absent, and A18 says “the import may then be made again.”
open_points.question: Does the one-import rule apply to the installation’s real lifetime or only to the currently restored store history?
options: The historical first success closes import permanently, even after restore
A restore before the closure permits another successful import
An external durable marker survives store restoration and keeps import closed
open_points.default_guess: Apply the rule to the restored store history, so the import is allowed again when the closure is absent.

open_points.subject: A10 ordering of agent calls against access changes
open_points.text: A10 says a call is accepted if its “transaction commits before the change” and refused if it “commits after it,” but agent reads do not store a change and the text names no commit or linearization point for them.
open_points.question: At what exact point is a read ordered against a concurrent revocation, archive or session end?
options: When the read transaction obtains its snapshot
When authorization is checked
When the answer is completed
Serialize every read with access-changing transactions
open_points.default_guess: Use the authorization check within a single read transaction as the read’s linearization point.

open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie scope
open_points.text: The cookie is described as “sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine” and “only to Registry’s own origin,” but no host, domain, path, SameSite or local-HTTP rules are stated, and browser cookies are not scoped by port as an origin is.
open_points.question: Which cookie attributes and deployment hostname/path make the cookie available only to Registry, including when the owner uses the interface locally?
options: Host-only, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict on a dedicated Registry hostname
Host-only and HttpOnly, allowing non-Secure loopback use
A narrowly scoped cookie path on a shared hostname
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated hostname with a host-only, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie and HTTPS everywhere.

open_points.subject: A13 failed confirmation submission
open_points.text: A13 says a confirmation is “used up by the first submission, whatever its answer,” but also describes “a value bound to another action” as used up without saying whether a missing, random, expired or already-replaced submitted value clears the one pending confirmation stored in the session.
open_points.question: After valid session and CSRF checks, exactly which refused submissions consume or clear the session’s pending confirmation?
options: Every confirmation submission clears the pending confirmation
Only submission of the exact pending value clears it, even if expired or wrongly bound
Only a valid, unexpired and correctly bound value is consumed
open_points.default_guess: Any submission carrying the exact pending value clears it after session and CSRF checks, even when it is expired or bound to the wrong submitted action; a random value does not clear it.

open_points.subject: A16 import file digest
open_points.text: The mapping, confirmation, migration closure and audit entry identify the file by “its digest,” but the digest algorithm and the exact bytes or canonical representation digested are not declared.
open_points.question: How is the import file digest computed so that mapping, confirmation, closure and audit always identify the same file and collision substitution is infeasible?
options: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a specified cryptographic algorithm
Digest a canonical parsed representation
Let each backend choose its digest and canonicalization
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 over the exact uploaded byte sequence.

open_points.subject: A16 uploaded import file storage
open_points.text: A16 says the file is “kept in the owner session ... never in the store” until replacement, acceptance or session end, but does not say whether it is held in memory or a temporary file, what permissions isolate it, or how remnants are removed after a crash or restart.
open_points.question: Where and under what access, cleanup and crash-recovery rules is the uploaded personal-data file kept during the session?
options: Keep it only in memory
Keep it in a private encrypted temporary file removed on every terminal event and startup cleanup
Allow a backend-specific session store with stated isolation guarantees
open_points.default_guess: Keep it in a Registry-private temporary file with restrictive permissions, encrypted storage, atomic replacement and startup cleanup of abandoned files.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption and metadata integrity
open_points.text: A18 requires each backup to be “encrypted with the backup key” and leaves its instant, release, sequence and key digest readable without the key, but states neither an authenticated-encryption construction nor whether the readable metadata is cryptographically bound to the ciphertext.
open_points.question: What encryption, nonce, authentication and metadata-binding rules define a valid backup and prevent undetected ciphertext or metadata substitution?
options: Use a specified AEAD format and authenticate all readable metadata as associated data
Encrypt only the store and rely on the later store integrity check
Leave the cryptographic format to the backend
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD backup format with a fresh random nonce and all cleartext metadata authenticated as associated data.

open_points.subject: A18 backup audit sequence metadata
open_points.text: A18 records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and checks that “its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number,” while A15 keeps the last-ever sequence counter separately and may erase all entries preceding the erasure entry.
open_points.question: Does backup metadata record the greatest entry still present, the durable last-ever-issued counter, or both, and how is a backup with no audit entries checked?
options: Record only the maximum sequence still present, using zero when none exists
Record only the last-ever-issued counter
Record both the last-ever-issued counter and the maximum present entry
open_points.default_guess: Record both values and verify the durable counter separately from the greatest surviving audit entry.

open_points.subject: A18 post-restore reconciliation scope
open_points.text: Rule 10 says the owner “brings each Customer and project to the state the owner’s own record of the retention review gives for it now — erased, restricted, ended or not,” although restriction and relationship ending are Customer facts, and it does not enumerate project archive, anonymisation or whole deletion states or the ordering needed to recreate them.
open_points.question: Which exact post-backup changes must be replayed for Customers, projects and audit retention, and in what order when prerequisite lifecycle states are absent from the restored backup?
options: Replay only the four conditions literally named
Replay every retention-related action recorded outside Registry, including archive, anonymisation and deletion
Restore a complete external change journal rather than a current-state checklist
open_points.default_guess: Replay every retention-related final state, archiving a project first when required before anonymising or deleting it, then apply the latest audit cutoff.

open_points.subject: A18 enforcement of restore quarantine
open_points.text: Rule 10 requires an owner-only start and reconciliation “before configuring the tokens and starting it again,” but also says Registry “cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done.”
open_points.question: What prevents service tokens from being enabled and the restored stale data served before the required reconciliation is complete?
options: Rely solely on the owner’s operational procedure
Persist a restore-pending marker that only an explicit owner completion action clears
Require a separate deployment mode that cannot load service tokens until reconciliation is certified
open_points.default_guess: Persist a restore-pending marker and refuse service-token configuration until the owner explicitly completes reconciliation.

open_points.subject: A18 repeat import source after restore
open_points.text: A18 says that when a pre-import backup is restored, “the import may then be made again, which restores” the imported records, while A16 drops the uploaded file after acceptance and State 0 retires the legacy source after migration; no text requires a recoverable copy of the accepted export to remain.
open_points.question: From where does the owner obtain the exact import file needed to repeat the migration after the original source and uploaded session file are gone?
options: The owner must retain the accepted export outside Registry for the backup-retention period
Registry must include an encrypted copy of the accepted export in backups
The legacy source must remain recoverable
The records are not recoverable by repeat import
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to retain an encrypted, integrity-checked copy of the accepted export outside Registry for as long as a restorable pre-import backup exists.

open_points.subject: A19 caller values and executable structure
open_points.text: The changed rule says “No value a caller gives ever becomes part of a query’s or a command’s structure; how the store’s backend lowers this is the backend’s,” without defining structure, distinguishing data from caller-supplied control values such as sort keys or artifact types, or stating what backend property verifies safe lowering.
open_points.question: Which caller-controlled values may select predefined query or command branches, and what exact rule proves that all remaining values cannot alter interpreted structure?
options: Only closed-enum control fields may select prewritten branches; all data values use backend-native parameter binding
Any backend escaping mechanism is acceptable if round-trip tests pass
Require a typed query API that cannot represent caller-supplied structure
Leave the distinction entirely to each backend
open_points.default_guess: Allow validated closed-enum controls to select prewritten branches and require every data value to pass through a backend-native parameter or typed-value API.

open_points.subject: A21 injection security-review conclusion
open_points.text: A21 defines the category as “no input becomes query, command, template or other interpreted structure” and marks it complete by reference to A19, but changed A19 speaks only of a query’s or command’s structure and its required tests only verify storage and HTML escaping, not structural non-interference or other interpreters.
open_points.question: What accepted rule and required tests cover templates and every other interpreted sink, and verify the backend-specific lowering that A19 now delegates?
options: Expand A19 and its tests to every interpreted sink
Narrow A21’s claimed category outcome to the sinks actually covered
Add a backend conformance requirement and injection test suite
open_points.default_guess: Expand A19 with a backend conformance rule and tests for query, command, template and other interpreter boundaries before retaining A21’s complete outcome.
